ai.description: This frog reaches 30–40 mm. It is brown with dark dorsal mottling and a distinct light vertebral stripe. Key features include a pointed snout and a prominent, continuous glandular fold on the dorsum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Fejervarya jhilmilensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous mid-dorsal white stripe extending from the snout to the vent.
ai.habitat: *Fejervarya jhilmilensis* inhabits marshy wetlands and grassy meadows within the Himalayan foothills, typically found at elevations between 250 and 350 meters.
ai.behavior: *Fejervarya jhilmilensis* is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to actively forage for small insects and invertebrates in damp, marshy habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Fejervarya jhilmilensis* reproduces via external fertilization in water, laying large clutches of eggs during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Fejervarya jhilmilensis* is endemic to the Jhilmil Jheel Conservation Reserve in the Haridwar district of Uttarakhand, India, occurring at low elevations.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Fejervarya jhilmilensis* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed notes emitted from the edges of marshy wetlands and rice paddies.
